bio.en: Teaser_2021 is a short promotional teaser episode with no single guest, used to preview the podcast and its upcoming conversations.
bio.zh: Teaser_2021 是一期短小的宣传预告节目，没有单一嘉宾，用于预告本播客及其即将推出的对话。

summary.en: This is a brief teaser episode that previews the kinds of guests and topics featured on the podcast rather than a full interview. It highlights the show's focus on product, growth, and career lessons from world-class operators. Listeners can treat it as a trailer for the broader series.
summary.zh: 这是一期简短的预告节目，预览了本播客所邀嘉宾与话题的类型，而非完整访谈。它突出了节目对产品、增长，以及来自世界级从业者的职业经验的聚焦。听众可将其视为整个系列的一支预告片。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: I'm Greg Isenberg and I build community. I'm the CEO of Late Checkout, an agency, a studio, a fund where we build some of the most popular internet communities. I'm also an advisor to Reddit.
turns.zh: 我是格雷格·伊森伯格，我致力于构建社区。我是Late Checkout的首席执行官，这是一家集代理公司、创意工作室和基金于一体的机构，我们在这里打造了许多广受欢迎的互联网社区。我同时也是Reddit的顾问。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: I'm Sahil Bloom. I'm an investor, creator, entrepreneur, writer. I also gave up a grand slam on ESPN in 2012, and I am still waiting for it to land. What is The Room Where it Happens? The Room Where it Happens is the place where the insights are generated. This is the place where the conversations happen, where ideas are batted around, debated, fought over. This is where things actually get created, where you start to have those seeds that are planted and where things are really built. That is the room. It's traditionally been closed. We're opening the door to it. We want you to be here with us as that happens.
turns.zh: 我是萨希尔·布鲁姆。我是投资者、创始人、企业家、作家。我还在2012年在ESPN上错失了一次重大机会，至今仍在等待它落地。《创意诞生之室》是什么？这是一个产生洞见的地方。这里是展开对话的场所，是思维碰撞、激烈辩论、争执不休的场所。这里是真正创造事物的地方，是播下种子、孕育新生、最终成型的场所。这就是创意诞生之室。传统上它是封闭的，但我们正在将它向外开放。我们希望在这一切发生时，你能与我们同在。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: It's a place where we could have honest conversations about how hard startups are, what's interesting to us, how we can collaborate, how we can build businesses together and what the next big thing is. That's what The Room Where it Happens is.
turns.zh: 在这里，我们可以坦诚地谈论创业的艰辛、感兴趣的领域、如何合作、共同打造事业，以及下一个重大机遇所在。这就是创意诞生之室的意义。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: If this podcast were available five years ago for me, I think I would've meaningfully accelerated the trajectory of my own life and my career. And part of that would've been the insights generated. The things I learned from actually listening to people. But the biggest part of it would've been the people I met. The relationships I built with other community members with the hosts, with the guests. That is what is the force multiplier for your career, those networks, how that compounds over time, just as well as any financial investment. That is what I would've gotten out of it.
turns.zh: 如果五年前有这个播客，我相信我的人生和事业轨迹会大大加速。其中很重要的一点是它带来的洞见——从倾听他人发声中获得的启发。但最重要的收获是结识的人脉，与其他社区成员、主持人、嘉宾建立的关系。这些人脉正是事业发展的倍增器，它们会随着时间累积，就像财务投资一样。这才是我能从中获得的真正价值。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: I probably would've met my co-founder. I probably would've met my early teammates. I probably would've found community. I would be 25 times more informed and 50 times more wealthy. That would've just supercharged my career.
turns.zh: 我很可能就此结识了我的联合创始人，遇到了早期团队成员，找到了归属感。我会比现在多获取25倍的信息，拥有50倍的财富。这将极大地推动我的职业生涯。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: Greg and I met in The Room Where it Happens. We met through the confluence of a bunch of chance events. We were in a group text thread together with a handful of friends and became as close as we are today because of that. It was The Room Where it Happens. All of these ideas were being generated and that was what sparked us, originally, to start thinking about this and thinking about how we could scale this so that more of you could be a part of what we had experienced and what we had benefited from.
turns.zh: 我和格雷格就是在创意诞生之室相识的。我们通过一系列偶然事件走到一起。我们曾与几个朋友在群聊中互动，正因如此，我们才变得如此亲密。这就是创意诞生之室。这里诞生了无数创意，这也最初激发了我们思考如何将其规模化，让更多人能分享我们的经历和受益。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: The moment that changed my mind about business and opportunity was the first time I ever went to Silicon Valley. I was reading up about all these entrepreneurs, all these investors on places like TechCrunch. And I landed and I expected them to be incredibly great, so much different from you and I. And I started having conversations with them and I realized they weren't smarter than us. They might have had better connections, more money, gone to better schools, but that was it. That was when I realized I could do anything.
turns.zh: 改变我对商业和机遇看法的转折点，是我第一次去硅谷的经历。我在TechCrunch等平台上阅读了许多创业者和投资者的故事。抵达后，我以为他们会无比卓越，与我们相差悬殊。但与他们交谈后，我意识到他们并不比我们更聪明。他们或许有更优质的人脉、更多的资金、更好的教育背景，但仅此而已。就在那时，我意识到自己可以做成任何事。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: So a moment that changed my mind about all of this, about business, opportunity, everything, I got invited by a mentor to go to a fundraiser event. I was 24. I was fresh out of school, very green. And I went to this event. There were all these amazing people there, really impressive people that I was, frankly, quite intimidated by. And I was in these conversations with them and just very quickly realized that there was nothing different about them versus me, but they were in these rooms constantly. They were around different, interesting people. They were having these conversations and that was what was making them different. They were able to generate these insights because they were in these room. And that was the moment I realized I had to just find a way to be in those rooms.
turns.zh: 让我举个例子，改变我对商业、机遇等一切看法的时刻。当时我24岁，刚毕业不久，经验不足。一次导师邀请我参加筹款活动。我到场后，那里全是令人惊叹的人物——他们才华横溢、令人敬畏。我与他们交谈后很快意识到，他们与我并没有什么不同，但他们总能出入各种高端场合，与形形色色的人交流。正是这种社交环境，让他们变得与众不同。他们能在这种环境中产生深刻洞见，而这正是我意识到自己必须找到进入这些圈子的方法的时刻。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: The gap between what people think business is and what actually happens is what Scott Belsky calls the messy middle. Think of The Social Network, the movie. Mark Zuckerberg starts Facebook and then all of a sudden it's massive. It's this romantic idea that people have about startups and entrepreneurship. In reality, the messy middle, the time in between starting and the outcome is 99% of the process of business and startups and entrepreneurship. And I actually find that messy middle to be the most amount of fun. It's when you rise up, it's when you fall down, it's when you zig and it's when you zag.
turns.zh: 斯科特·贝尔斯基将人们对商业的认知与实际情况之间的差距称为"混沌中段"。想想电影《社交网络》吧。马克·扎克伯格创立Facebook后，公司迅速壮大。这是人们对初创公司和创业精神的浪漫想象。但现实中，从创业到成功的这段混沌中段，却占据了商业和创业过程的99%。我发现这个阶段最具挑战性，也是最有趣的时刻——它关乎你如何崛起、如何倒下、如何曲折前行。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: So in my mind, the biggest gap between what people think business is versus what it really is, is that aspect of just crawling through the river of shit that exists between where you start and where you finish. It's like The Shawshank Redemption. You got to just go through that period. And to me, that's getting up every day and just getting punched in the gut over and over and over again, and being willing to get up and continue to push through and continue to work with your team, solicit feedback, work with others and just get through it. But that willingness to get punched in the face, to get knocked down and to get back up, no one talks about that. Everyone talks about the successes. You love the glamor you love when someone rings the bell at the New York Stock Exchange, when they IPO, they're billionaire, it's great. (05:23): No one talks about that middle time when you're just getting punched over and over and over again. What frustrates me most about the current state of podcasts is just that it's one sided. It all ends as soon as you finish the conversation during the interview. It's an interview, you talk to someone, you ask them questions and then it ends and that's it. That's all you get from them. And they might have said something amazing that intrigued you, that sparked your interest. You want to follow up, you want to dig deeper, but that's it. That's all you get and it's over. And so when I think about the opportunity that exists, it's changing that. Fundamentally flipping it on its head, making it a conversation, following up, digging deeper, going further with all the insights. That's how we take this entire thing to a whole new level.
turns.zh: 在我看来，人们对商业认知与现实的最大差距，就在于如何穿越从创业到成功之间那条充斥着泥泞与障碍的河流。这就像《肖申克的救赎》——你必须经历那个阶段。对我而言，这意味着每天清晨醒来，面对接连不断的打击，仍能振作起来，继续与团队合作、收集反馈、寻求他人的帮助，最终渡过难关。但这种愿意接受打击、跌倒后再爬起的韧性，鲜少被提及。人们只谈论成功——你喜欢纽交所敲响钟声的光环，IPO时的狂喜，亿万富翁的身份，皆大欢喜。（05:23）但无人谈及那段备受煎熬的中间阶段——你不断遭遇打击却无处求助。当下播客生态的问题在于，它太过单向。采访结束，嘉宾离开，所有信息都戛然而止。采访不过是双方的对谈，你提问对方，结束后就再无后续。这就是为什么当我思考机遇时，首先要颠覆现有模式——将对话转为持续交流，追问深层见解，深挖潜在价值。唯有如此，我们才能将整个生态推向新高度。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: I believe the current state of podcasting sucks. A few people have microphones and it's just not fair. What if you allowed a bunch of people to have microphones so they could connect, so they can collaborate so that they can build community. And that's what we're trying to do with The Room Where it Happens. Yes, we're in the room and we have some microphones, but we're also inviting you in. We want you to ask questions. We want to collaborate with you. We want to build businesses with you. And that's why I wanted to create a new, more modern way of podcasting. What am I most excited about with this show and community?
turns.zh: 我认为当前的播客生态实在糟糕。只有少数人能拥有麦克风，这太不公平了。要是能让更多人获得麦克风，让他们建立联系、展开合作、共同构建社区，那该多好？这正是我们打造《发生之屋》节目的初衷。没错，我们身处演播室，手握麦克风，但我们也诚挚邀请您加入其中。我们希望您能提出问题，与我们携手合作，共创事业。这就是我为何要开创一种全新的、更现代的播客模式。我对这档节目和社区最期待的是什么？

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: It has to be seeing the amazing things that come out of this community. It has to be seeing all of you going off and having these great experiences, having new insights that come from it, starting new things, failing, succeeding, all of that. And what it's going to create out in the world is what I'm most excited about. We get to sit here, have conversations. We get to hang out with friends, talk to some amazing guests, but the thing that's going to be best is when we see you take that and run with it 100 times over to create something much bigger than what we are doing here.
turns.zh: 最让我激动的，是见证这个社区创造出的惊人成果。看着各位大展身手、收获深刻见解、开启新篇章、经历失败与成功……这些改变世界的力量才是我最向往的。我们可以坐在一起畅谈，结交好友，邀请嘉宾分享智慧，但最振奋人心的，是看着你们将这些能量百倍放大，创造出远超我们想象的奇迹。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: Watching where you are today and where you're going to be tomorrow and where you're going to be a week from now, a month, a year, 10 years. We're in this for the long game. And what excites me about... I mean, the reason why I got into community was because I love seeing people progress, advance, do big things. And I know that being a part of The Room Where it Happens, good things will happen to you.
turns.zh: 观察你们当下的处境、未来的方向、一周后、一个月后、一年后、十年后的模样。我们要以长远的眼光投入其中。让我兴奋的……说到底，我投身社区建设的初衷，就是见证人们进步、成长、成就非凡。加入《发生之屋》这个大家庭，必将为你们带来丰厚的回报。

turns.speaker: Sahil Bloom
turns.en: So how are we going to ensure this is different than everything else out there? Two ways. Number one, alcohol. We're going to get everyone really drunk with us and it's going to be fun and we're going to get them loose. Because they're not going to be having the same conversation they're having on to every single other podcast, because they're going to be sitting there drinking with us and it's going to be fun. So that's number one. Number two, we want to learn from you. We want to get better at this. We're in it for the long game. This isn't one episode, this isn't one season. We're going to be doing it. So when you're hearing things, if you want us to improve on stuff, if you have ideas, episodes, be a part of it with us, tell us, message us. You're in the Discord, be there with us, help us improve as we grow, and we'll make sure that it is the best thing that we can possibly create.
turns.zh: 那么，如何确保我们的节目与众不同？两个关键点：第一，酒精。我们要把大家灌得烂醉，营造轻松氛围，让他们放开自我。因为他们不会像在其他播客节目中那样拘谨——毕竟他们正与我们举杯畅饮，享受欢乐时光。所以这第一招奏效了。第二，我们要向你们学习。我们要在实践中精进。我们要长远布局。这不是一期节目，也不是一个季度的尝试。我们将持续深耕。因此，当你们听到节目内容时，若有改进建议，若有创意想法，若想参与节目制作，请随时告知我们。加入我们的Discord社区，助力我们共同成长，我们定会打造出最完美的作品。

turns.speaker: Greg Isenberg
turns.en: And you're going to keep us on us. You're going to be in our Discord. You're going to be in our community. And if anything feels not authentic, not great, we're in this together, and we want to make this as authentic as possible.
turns.zh: 而你们要监督我们。加入我们的Discord社区，融入我们的生态。若有任何不真诚、不精彩之处，我们将携手共进，力求让一切尽善尽美。
